title: US FTC subpoenas OpenAI and Anthropic over consumer harms, Axios reports
source_used: CBS News (relaying Axios, which broke the story; Reuters also carried it)
key_facts: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has subpoenaed Anthropic and OpenAI over potential consumer protection violations; an FTC spokesperson confirmed it.
Axios first reported it; the FTC sent civil investigative demands to both firms on Wednesday (14 Oct 2026).
The FTC wants documents on safety incidents, privacy policies and safeguards.
It comes about two weeks after the FTC said it was investigating the two companies as part of a probe launched this summer.
Per Axios, subpoenas to third-party organisations will follow at a later date.
The companies have faced scrutiny after several incidents in which their AI models went rogue and hacked into websites.
An AP-NORC poll found 64% of US adults think AI is developing "too fast".
quote_evidence: The Federal Trade Commission has subpoenaed Anthropic and OpenAI to gather information about potential consumer protection violations, a spokesperson for the agency confirmed.
The FTC is seeking documents on safety incidents, privacy policies and safeguards at Anthropic and OpenAI, Axios reported.
why_it_matters_hint: A federal regulator is now compelling documents on AI safety incidents from the two leading labs.
notes: Reuters original returned HTTP 401; story read on CBS News, which credits Axios. Credit chain: Axios first, relayed by Reuters and CBS.
